interventions.speaker: REGISTRAR
interventions.who: the registrar who pulls up documents; reports what they say, nothing else
interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI prostate demonstrated a focal lesion in the peripheral zone at the right base, measuring approximately 18 x 15 mm. The lesion was markedly hypointense on T2WI, showed restricted diffusion with high signal on b=1400 and low ADC values, and demonstrated early, intense enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences. No extracapsular extension or lymphadenopathy was identified. Impression was PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right base of the prostate, with PSA density of 0.333 ng/mL/mL and clinical T stage cT2.
**pathology_report**: Histological examination of the prostate tissue revealed acinar adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. High-risk patterns included a cribriform pattern and intraductal carcinoma (IDC-P). Perineural invasion was identified. The tumour was located at the base, right.
**previous_notes**: Prior notes indicate an initial biopsy in February 2023 confirmed Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2, with perineural invasion. A follow-up in June 2024 noted a PSA rise to 5.4 ng/mL and moderate LUTS.
**family_history**: No family history of prostate cancer was recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trend shows an increase from 2.6 ng/mL in April 2023 to 7.8 ng/mL in February 2025, with intermediate values of 3.7 ng/mL (Nov 2023) and 5.4 ng/mL (Jul 2024).
**laboratory_results**: The most recent PSA was 7.8 ng/mL (24 Dec 2024). Free PSA was 1.04 ng/mL (13%), and the eGFR was >60 mL/min/1.73m2.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific details requested by the moderator regarding the MRI findings (beyond the impression), the full pathological details regarding extracapsular extension or nodal involvement (beyond perineural invasion), and any further context from the urology consultation regarding the LUTS or shoulder pain are not fully detailed in the retrieved documents.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
The retrieved documents strongly support the high-risk nature of this case. The PI-RADS 5 finding on MRI, combined with the positive biopsy showing Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2, and perineural invasion, places the patient in a high-risk category. The rising PSA trend further supports the need for definitive management planning.
